title: Which count can't drift?
prompt: The Watchlist header shows how many movies are still unwatched. Users can add movies, remove them and mark them watched. **Pick every design where the header can never disagree with the list.**
hints: Ask of each design: is there a second copy of the number that someone has to remember to update?
A value calculated from the list every time it's shown has no second copy to forget.
explanation: The two correct designs both **derive** the count from the list whenever the screen is drawn, so there is only one source of truth: the array of movies. The other two keep a second copy of the number (in a variable or in the DOM) and rely on every handler, now and in the future, to update it correctly. That is exactly the bookkeeping React is designed to remove.

derive-in-render.text: The header calculates `movies.filter((m) => !m.watched).length` each time it renders.
derive-in-render.why: Correct. The number is recalculated from the list on every render, so there is nothing separate to keep in sync.

counter-variable.text: A `leftCount` variable starts at the list length, and each click handler adds or subtracts 1.
counter-variable.why: This keeps a second copy of the truth. Forget to adjust it in one handler (say, removing a watched movie) and the header is wrong.

read-dom.text: Each handler reads the number currently shown in the header, changes it and writes it back.
read-dom.why: The DOM becomes the source of truth, and any handler that forgets to touch it leaves the screen out of sync with the data.

derive-in-child.text: A `WatchCount` component receives the movie list and computes the number itself.
derive-in-child.why: Correct. It's the same idea moved into its own component: the count comes from the list, never from a separate tally.
